title: TIME divides total_seconds by 86400 before taking the fractional day, so TIME(25,0,0) differs by 11 ULP from 1/24
statement: In Excel 16.0.20527.20088, TIME(hour, minute, second) truncates each argument, checks each |arg| <= 32767 and total_seconds >= 0 (returning #NUM! for negative total seconds such as TIME(0,-1,0)), and evaluates frac(total_seconds / 86400). Because 25*3600/86400 = 1 + 1/24 loses 11 bits when the integer day 1 is subtracted, TIME(25,0,0) returns 0.04166666666666674 (0x3fa5555555555560), 11 ULP above 1/24 (0x3fa5555555555555).
basis: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527.20088 in f2_rows (rows 106-108) and matched across 1,296/1,296 full-bank and 120/120 pinned TIME rows in Excel 16.0.20430.

correct.how: Exact rational 1/24 rounded to nearest binary64
